source_snapshot.test_name_items: PCIe slot check ( x16 on slot 1 to 10)
source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    Check PCIe device (x16 width on slot 1 to 10) in BIOS setup menu, uEFI shell and OS
Check PCIe link status (Speed and Width).
 In uEFI shell:
  Send command: "pci". Check PCIe information (add "i" parameter for more information from PCIe device)
 In Linux:
  Send command: "lspci vvv". Check PCIe information.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria:
1. PCIe device information should show correctly in BIOS, uEFI shell and OS
2. Link status and speed should match the SPEC definition.

deepseek_columns.ai_commands: -- PCIe slot check (x16 on slot 1 to 10): agent can auto-dump the OS-side PCIe device+link info sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "lspci -vvv 2>&1 | grep -Ei 'LnkCap|LnkSta|Region' | head -n 80; echo '---devices---'; lspci 2>&1" ; the BIOS setup-menu and uEFI shell pci output are read by the operator.
deepseek_columns.ai_logs_output: return lspci -vvv LnkCap/LnkSta + the PCIe device list so the operator confirms widths/speeds on slots 1..10 match SPEC; the BIOS/uEFI-shell views are operator-read.

original_test_intent: Verify expected PCIe devices in physical slots 1 through 10 across BIOS setup, UEFI shell and Linux, and confirm each negotiated link width and speed matches the platform specification.
original_method: Use the motherboard slot/root-port map to inspect each populated slot in BIOS, run the firmware `pci` detail view in UEFI, collect full Linux `lspci -vvv` data, and reconcile device identity, speed and width across all three environments.
manual_activity: An operator must enter and inspect BIOS setup and UEFI shell, preserve console captures and return the system to its normal boot path. The Linux inventory and comparison can be automated after the physical-slot map is supplied.
required_inputs: Motherboard revision and slots 1-10 to root-port/BDF mapping
Expected device/vendor/device/serial population and required generation/speed/width per slot
BIOS/UEFI navigation and `pci` syntax for the installed firmware
Approved reboot window, console/OOB recovery, pciutils version and one-user approval
safety_requirements: Keep OS collection read-only; do not bind/unbind, remove/rescan, retrain or change PCIe settings.
Do not reboot or enter firmware without approval and a tested return-to-OS path.
Capture full evidence before filtering so absent devices or downgraded links are not hidden.
Stop on device loss, AER/fatal errors, boot-path change or recovery failure; do not auto-retry.
agent_execution_scope: Collect full Linux PCI inventory, configuration and link capabilities/status for mapped BDFs.
Ingest operator BIOS/UEFI captures and reconcile the same device/slot across views.
Flag missing devices and speed/width downgrades against the supplied SPEC, leaving the verdict to the engineer.
engineer_actions: Supply the physical-slot map, expected population and per-slot link SPEC.
Perform BIOS/UEFI navigation and capture the firmware evidence.
Approve reboot/recovery and issue the formal verdict.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Only partially applicable. `lspci -vvv` is appropriate for Linux, but `grep ... | head -n 80` can omit devices and cannot map slots 1-10 without an owner topology; password-in-command SSH handling is also unsuitable.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Preserve the source firmware `pci`/detail inspection and use complete `lspci -nn -D -vvv` output or the approved pciutils equivalent in Linux. The literal source text `lspci vvv` is syntactically incomplete and must not be executed as written.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Slots 1-10, x16 target context, BIOS/UEFI/Linux views, speed/width checks and both five-minute fields are preserved.

modernized_recommendation.status: CORRECT SYNTAX AND ADD TOPOLOGY-BOUND EVIDENCE
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Capture full domain-qualified Linux enumeration and verbose link data, map each BDF to the supplied physical slot/root port, then compare with labeled BIOS and UEFI captures from the same boot cycle.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: The specified motherboard revision and installed PCIe topology.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record pciutils, UEFI shell, BIOS, BMC and device firmware versions.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Installed pciutils help/man output plus owner BIOS/UEFI and motherboard slot documentation; no new control command is introduced.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Corrects missing option hyphens and makes cross-view identity explicit.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Preserves all three required views and avoids DeepSeek's truncation.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Slot map, expected population and per-slot link SPEC.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: OS BDF numbering may differ across firmware configuration or boots; physical mapping must be independently anchored.

project_override_considerations: A project can define which slots are populated and their negotiated width/speed, including intentional bifurcation or downgrade. The report must state the approved map and cannot claim unused or unobserved slots were validated.
expected_evidence: SUT/motherboard/firmware identity, slot-root-port-BDF map and expected population/SPEC
Complete Linux PCI inventory and per-device capability/status without truncation
Labeled BIOS and UEFI captures for the same slots/devices
Cross-view comparison, AER/system/SEL logs, boot recovery and separate engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The three environments and speed/width criterion are consistent. The malformed Linux option spelling is a command defect, not a contradiction in test intent.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Topology, SPEC, package and console access are project readiness inputs. Firmware observation makes the case partial, but nothing requires permanent BLOCKED status.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Retain partial classification and OS collection, but reject truncation, guessed SSH handling and unmapped slot conclusions.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Agree with REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION and its full cross-view mapping and reboot controls.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.v3_1_improvement: Explicitly separates the malformed legacy command from the preserved method and prevents OS evidence from substituting for firmware views.

review_improvement: Establishes slot identity before comparison, preserves unfiltered evidence and retains BIOS/UEFI coverage rather than reducing the case to an OS inventory.
independent_technical_reasoning: Link capability/status is machine-readable in Linux, but the source explicitly requires two pre-OS views. Those views involve reboot/navigation and cannot be inferred from `lspci`. Because hardware setup is not itself the core yet firmware inspection is manual, the V3.1 PARTIAL label is appropriate.
